title_en: Chen Bangrong, Chen Guorong, Chen Xi v. Chen Jing, Wu Jianping, Li Yueguo, Zhou Fuyong — dispute over the right to life
ruling_gist_en: Creditors who take self-help measures within reasonable limits to prevent the debtor from again concealing and evading debts, and who agree with the debtor to go together to a people's court to resolve the debt dispute, during which the debtor, without being under any real threat to personal safety, voluntarily climbs out of a window and flees in order to continue evading the legal debt, resulting in death, shall not bear legal liability.
keywords_en: Civil; dispute over right to life; first instance; basic people's court; Chongqing Municipality; natural person; Civil Code; reasonable limits of self-help; whether the creditor bears tort liability; attribution of liability for debtor's death by voluntarily climbing out of window; dismissal of claims; debt collection; self-help; death by falling from window; good faith; Zhou Fuyong right to life dispute
full_text_en:
Chen Bangrong, Chen Guorong, and Chen Xi v.
Chen Jing, Wu Jianping, Li Yueguo, and Zhou Fuyong — dispute over right to life

Ruling Summary

Where a creditor adopts self-help measures within reasonable limits to prevent a debtor from again concealing assets and evading debts, and agrees with the debtor to go together to a people’s court to resolve the debt dispute, and during this period the debtor, without facing any real threat to his or her personal safety, chooses to flee by climbing out of a window in order to continue evading the legal debt, resulting in death, the creditor bears no legal liability.

Plaintiffs: Chen Bangrong, female, 44 years old, Han Chinese, residing in Yubei District, Chongqing.
Plaintiffs: Chen Guorong, male, 76 years old, Han Chinese, residing in Yubei District, Chongqing.
Plaintiffs: Chen Xi, female, 19 years old, Han Chinese, residing in Yubei District, Chongqing.

Defendants: Chen Jing, female, 46 years old, Han Chinese, residing in Yubei District, Chongqing.
Defendants: Wu Jianping, male, 46 years old, Han Chinese, residing in Yubei District, Chongqing.
Defendants: Li Yueguo, male, 30 years old, Han Chinese, residing in Yubei District, Chongqing.
Defendants: Zhou Fuyong, male, 36 years old, Han Chinese, residing in Jiangbei District, Chongqing.

The plaintiffs, Chen Bangrong, Chen Guorong, and Chen Xi, filed an action with the Yubei District People’s Court of Chongqing against the defendants, Chen Jing, Wu Jianping, Li Yueguo, and Zhou Fuyong, concerning a dispute over the right to life.

The plaintiffs, Chen Bangrong, Chen Guorong, and Chen Xi, alleged: In the early morning of September 28, 2017, the defendant Chen Jing, together with the defendants Wu Jianping and Li Yueguo, among others, came to collect a debt, trapping Chen Jian in a KTV and preventing him from leaving, and also summoned some idle persons from society to threaten Chen Jian, causing him great mental stress and suffering. Chen Jian, having no choice, went to the Huixing Police Station to seek protection. At around 2:00 a.m., Chen Jing left, while Wu Jianping and Li Yueguo remained to continue controlling Chen Jian. Even when Chen Jian went to the restroom on the second floor of the nearby Fanghua Hospital, he was watched and followed by Wu Jianping and Li Yueguo. At 5:44 a.m., while tired, hungry, and in a state of extreme fear, tension, and anxiety, Chen Jian, in an attempt to break free from control, fell from a height when going to the restroom for the third time due to the negligence of Wu Jianping and Li Yueguo. Chen Jian later died despite rescue efforts. The plaintiffs repeatedly contacted the defendants to negotiate a settlement but failed. Therefore, they filed this lawsuit in accordance with the law, requesting the court to order the four defendants to jointly and severally compensate the three plaintiffs for medical expenses of RMB 70,165.40, hospital meal subsidies of RMB 150, transportation expenses of RMB 90, nutrition expenses of RMB 300, death compensation of RMB 592,200, funeral expenses of RMB 32,772.50, and living expenses for dependents of RMB 9,871, totaling 60% of the above amounts, plus mental distress damages of RMB 100,000.

The defendants Chen Jing and Wu Jianping argued: First, there was no physical contact between the defendants and the deceased. Throughout the entire process of negotiating the debt, both parties spoke in a friendly manner, and there was no threat or coercion as claimed by the plaintiffs. Second, when the defendants asserted their creditor’s rights, they first called the police and then contacted the court, and later both parties went to the nearby police station to resolve the matter. This series of actions was entirely lawful. When the deceased went to the restroom, Wu Jianping was always in the corridor, and from the restroom to the place where the deceased fell, it was necessary to climb out of a window and walk across a color steel plate. Therefore, the defendants could not have anticipated the deceased’s fall, and thus the defendants were not at fault. Third, the defendant Chen Jing had already left the scene at the time of the incident and was unaware of the entire event, so the plaintiffs’ claim against Chen Jing lacks factual basis. Fourth, the facts alleged by the plaintiffs are not established: (1) the defendants did not restrict the deceased’s personal freedom; (2) it was the defendant Zhou Fuyong who voluntarily reported the case that night, not the deceased reporting under duress; (3) the defendants did not threaten the deceased or cause him mental suffering; (4) the deceased was in a state of freedom throughout the entire process. At the police station, the defendants owed no duty of care to the deceased, and there was no claim of failure to ensure safety. In summary, they requested the dismissal of the plaintiffs’ claims.

The defendant Li Yueguo argued: The statements in the plaintiffs’ complaint are untrue. Li Yueguo did not trap the deceased in the KTV. At that time, Li Yueguo had just arrived at the KTV and did not even go upstairs before going to the police station together.

The defendant Zhou Fuyong argued: There is no basis for the plaintiffs to sue Zhou Fuyong, and Zhou Fuyong should not bear any liability.

The Yubei District People’s Court of Chongqing found the following facts at first instance:

The plaintiff Chen Bangrong is the wife of Chen Jian, the plaintiff Chen Guorong is the father of Chen Jian, and the plaintiff Chen Xi is the daughter of Chen Jian. The defendant Chen Jing had previously filed a lawsuit against Liu Ping (Chen Jian’s ex-wife) and Chen Jian on October 8, 2013, regarding Liu Ping’s failure to repay a loan, in the Yubei District People’s Court of Chongqing. After trial, the Yubei District People’s Court issued Civil Judgment (2013) Yubei Fa Min Chu Zi No. 15888, ordering Liu Ping and Chen Jian to jointly repay the loan principal of RMB 470,000 plus interest to Chen Jing. After the judgment became effective, Chen Jing applied for enforcement, and later Chen Jing and Liu Ping reached an enforcement settlement under the auspices of the Yubei District People’s Court of Chongqing, which mainly stipulated that Liu Ping would pay Chen Jing RMB 30,000 by December 31, 2014, and thereafter pay RMB 5,000 per month. If Liu Ping failed to perform on time, enforcement would resume. If Chen Jing discovered any executable property of Chen Jian, she could request enforcement against Chen Jian at any time. Thereafter, Chen Jing did not locate Chen Jian, and the creditor’s rights remained unrealized.

Until the evening of September 27, 2017, Chen Jing, along with the defendant Zhou Fuyong and others, was at the 365KTV on Huixing Street. During this time, Zhou Fuyong invited the defendant Li Yueguo by phone to drink. Around midnight on September 28, 2017, Chen Jing noticed Chen Jian and others settling their bill at the front desk. Chen Jing approached Chen Jian and demanded repayment. Chen Jian stated that he did not owe Chen Jing any money. Chen Jing then grabbed Chen Jian’s arm while calling her husband, the defendant Wu Jianping. Zhou Fuyong called the police. Subsequently, Wu Jianping arrived at the 365KTV with the relevant documents from the earlier case, and Li Yueguo also happened to arrive. During this time, Chen Jing tried to contact the judge in charge of the enforcement case but failed. Chen Jian, Chen Jing, and others agreed to go to the nearby Huixing Police Station to resolve the matter. Accordingly, Chen Jing, Wu Jianping, Li Yueguo, Zhou Fuyong, Chen Jian, and his friend Wan Qihua went together to the Huixing Police Station and explained the situation to the staff. The staff stated that the economic dispute between the parties should be resolved through judicial channels. Both parties then agreed to wait until dawn and go together to the Yubei District People’s Court of Chongqing to resolve the matter.

Thereafter, Chen Jing and Zhou Fuyong left successively, leaving Wu Jianping, Li Yueguo, Chen Jian, and Wan Qihua at the police station. Subsequently, Wan Qihua also left. While waiting for dawn, Chen Jian went twice to the restroom at the nearby Chongqing Fanghua Hospital. Wu Jianping and Li Yueguo followed Chen Jian and waited outside the restroom. Around 5:00 a.m. on September 28, 2017, Chen Jian sent a message to Chen Bangrong stating that he was at the Huixing Police Station and that they would go to the court after dawn to resolve the debt matter involving Liu Ping, and asked Chen Bangrong to come and get the keys to withdraw money from the card. At around 5:30 a.m., Chen Jian went to the restroom at Chongqing Fanghua Hospital for the third time. Wu Jianping and Li Yueguo waited outside but did not see Chen Jian come out for a long time, so they began to look for him. Finally, they found Chen Jian lying on the road downstairs on the side of the restroom window wall. They contacted the police, who then contacted medical personnel. The medical personnel arrived and rushed Chen Jian to the hospital for rescue. Chen Jian died despite rescue efforts. For this reason, the plaintiffs incurred medical expenses of RMB 70,165.40.

The above facts were confirmed by the household registration booklet, marriage certificate, interrogation records, surveillance video, scene photos, medical records, medical expense receipts, and the statements of the parties.

The Yubei District People’s Court of Chongqing held at first instance:

The plaintiffs claimed that the defendants restricted Chen Jian’s personal freedom and caused him mental stress and suffering, leading Chen Jian to fall from a height while trying to break free from the defendants. The defendants denied restricting Chen Jian’s personal freedom or causing him mental stress. This was the focus of the dispute in the litigation.

A citizen’s creditor’s rights can be realized through both public relief and private relief. Chen Jing’s creditor’s rights were not actually satisfied even after a court judgment and enforcement. On the evening of September 27, 2017, Chen Jing accidentally encountered the debtor Chen Jian. She promptly called the police and sought public relief from the enforcement judge, and grabbed Chen Jian’s arm to demand repayment. The above actions of Chen Jing did not exceed reasonable limits and did not constitute a tort.

Based on the surveillance video from the scene and the interrogation records of relevant persons, from the time Chen Jing discovered Chen Jian until Wu Jianping arrived with the relevant proof of the debt, to when Chen Jing and others called the police and the enforcement judge, to when both parties went together to the Huixing Police Station to resolve the debt issue, and finally to when Wu Jianping, Li Yueguo, and Chen Jian waited together for dawn to go to the Yubei District People’s Court of Chongqing to resolve the debt dispute, there was no physical conflict between the parties. Chen Jian could move freely and send and receive text messages. Thus, there was no tortious conduct in this process.

Although Wu Jianping and Li Yueguo waited in the corridor outside the restroom when Chen Jian went to the restroom, their subjective purpose was to ensure that both parties could go to court after dawn to resolve the debt issue, not to obtain illegal benefits in this way. Therefore, Wu Jianping and Li Yueguo did not have the intent or negligence to infringe on Chen Jian’s personal interests. Objectively, after the court judgment, the deceased Chen Jian did not have the willingness or conduct to voluntarily perform the debt obligation. When encountering Chen Jing, he even denied the debt. Moreover, the court and the police could not resolve the debt dispute immediately at that time. Under these circumstances, Wu Jianping and Li Yueguo following Chen Jian to the restroom and waiting in the corridor to ensure that they could go to the court after dawn to resolve the debt dispute did not exceed the reasonable limits of self-help and did not constitute a tort.

Regarding the plaintiffs’ claim that the defendants’ conduct caused Chen Jian mental stress and suffering, the Yubei District People’s Court of Chongqing found that the specific environment where Chen Jian and Wu Jianping and Li Yueguo were located was the Huixing Police Station, with staff on duty nearby. Moreover, from the 365KTV to the time both parties sat in the police station waiting for dawn, there were no physical conflicts. The defendants’ purpose had been clearly expressed: to go together to the court after dawn to resolve the debt issue. Therefore, Chen Jian’s personal safety was not actually infringed upon. At the same time, the subjective purpose of Wu Jianping and others was to go to the court after dawn to resolve the debt dispute. Thus, Chen Jian was also not subjected to threats sufficient to endanger his personal safety. Accordingly, the Yubei District People’s Court of Chongqing did not support the plaintiffs’ claim. In summary, the defendants Wu Jianping and Li Yueguo did not commit any act infringing on Chen Jian’s rights and should not bear tort liability. The defendants Chen Jing and Zhou Fuyong left the Huixing Police Station first and committed no tortious acts, so they should not bear liability. Chen Jian, without facing any threat to his personal safety, used the opportunity of going to the restroom, knowing the danger, climbed out of the restroom window and left the scene, accidentally fell, and suffered a craniocerebral injury leading to death despite rescue efforts. His own fault was clear, and he should bear the responsibility himself.

Accordingly, the Yubei District People’s Court of Chongqing, in accordance with Article 6 of the Tort Law of the People’s Republic of China and Articles 64 and 144 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People’s Republic of China, rendered its judgment on February 5, 2018:

All claims of the plaintiffs Chen Bangrong, Chen Guorong, and Chen Xi were dismissed.

Chen Bangrong, Chen Guorong, and Chen Xi, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Chongqing No. 1 Intermediate People’s Court, arguing:

1. The four appellees’ illegal debt collection clearly exceeded the reasonable extent of self-help and should be characterized as a tort. The public security investigation records and surveillance video showed that the four appellees, to a certain extent, restricted Chen Jian’s range of activities and indirectly restricted his personal freedom, constituting illegal debt collection that clearly exceeded the reasonable extent of self-help. The trial court’s mere reliance on the absence of physical conflict to conclude that Chen Jian could move freely, and its reliance on the appellees’ unilateral subjective purpose to find no tortious conduct, constituted an incorrect characterization of the appellees’ conduct and improper application of the law. 2. The four appellees were at fault for Chen Jian’s death, and their fault was causally related to Chen Jian’s death from falling while evading the debt. The four appellees, to a certain extent, restricted Chen Jian’s personal freedom, as evidenced by their use of hitting, twisting, and other means to urge him to go to the police station and preventing him from leaving on his own. Because the four appellees restricted Chen Jian’s range of activities for a long time, Chen Jian tried to break free from control and fell to his death. Therefore, Chen Jian’s death was causally related to the appellees’ illegal debt collection, falling within the circumstances described in Article 6 of the Tort Law of the People’s Republic of China. Thus, the first-instance judgment found facts incorrectly and applied the law incorrectly. They requested the appellate court to reverse the original judgment and order the appellees to pay the appellants medical expenses, death compensation, funeral expenses, hospital meal subsidies, living expenses for dependents, nutrition expenses, transportation expenses, and mental distress damages totaling RMB 523,329.34; and to order the appellees to bear the litigation costs of the first and second instances.

The appellees Chen Jing and Wu Jianping argued: 1. The appellees’ method of asserting their creditor’s rights was entirely lawful and did not exceed the limits prescribed by law. The appellees strictly followed the information provided by the enforcement judge and the provisions of the law. From reporting to the police, contacting the judge, to going to the police station together, this series of actions did not violate any prohibitive provisions of the law and constituted a lawful assertion of creditor’s rights, falling within the scope of private relief provided by law. 2. The appellees did not have the subjective intent to infringe on Chen Jian’s personal rights. At the time of the incident, Wu Jianping was always in the corridor and did not enter the restroom. He only had the purpose of lawfully realizing the creditor’s rights and did not have the subjective intent to infringe on Chen Jian’s personal safety. 3. The appellees did not commit any tortious acts. There was no physical contact between the appellees and Chen Jian. Throughout the entire negotiation process, both parties were peaceful and friendly, with polite speech. The appellees never subjected Chen Jian to mental coercion, and the incident occurred at the police station. There were no threats, coercion, or similar facts as alleged by the appellants. The appellees did not restrict Chen Jian’s personal freedom; objectively, Chen Jian’s actions were free. 4. Chen Jing had already left at the time of the incident and was unaware of the entire event. Suing Chen Jing has no factual basis. In summary, the appellants’ appeal should not be sustained, and they requested the appellate court to affirm the original judgment.

The appellee Li Yueguo argued: The first-instance judgment correctly found the facts, and he bore no liability. He merely accompanied them to the police station and slept on a bench at the police station during the wait.

The appellee Zhou Fuyong argued: The first-instance judgment correctly found the facts, and he bore no liability. He had no physical contact with Chen Jian, merely called the police in the middle of it, and did not restrict Chen Jian’s personal freedom. He also left early after arriving at the police station. The appellants’ lawsuit against Zhou Fuyong constituted malicious litigation.

The Chongqing No. 1 Intermediate People’s Court, upon appellate review, confirmed the facts found at first instance.

The focus of the dispute in this case was: whether the conduct of the appellees Chen Jing and others constituted a tort and whether they should bear compensation liability.

The Chongqing No. 1 Intermediate People’s Court held at second instance: This case is a general tort case. According to the Tort Law of the People’s Republic of China, the elements of a general tort include a tortious act, fault, damage, and a causal relationship between the tortious act and the damage. When all four elements are satisfied, the actor shall bear tort liability.

Based on the facts found, the conduct of the appellees Chen Jing and others did not violate the law. The creditor-debtor relationship between Chen Jing and Chen Jian had been confirmed by an effective judgment. After Chen Jing applied for enforcement to the Yubei District People’s Court of Chongqing, Chen Jian had never performed his legal obligation. Several years later, when Chen Jing and Chen Jian met by chance, in order to protect the realization of the creditor’s rights and prevent Chen Jian from concealing himself again, the creditor Chen Jing held onto Chen Jian while making phone calls to seek help. The accompanying Zhou Fuyong called the police. While at the police station, Wu Jianping and Li Yueguo paid close attention to Chen Jian and followed him and waited outside when Chen Jian went to the restroom. However, there was never any physical conflict with Chen Jian. Moreover, all actions were aimed at getting the debtor Chen Jian, who had failed to repay the debt for years and was difficult to find, to fulfill his repayment obligation. There was no purpose or motive to infringe on Chen Jian’s lawful rights and interests. From the text message Chen Jian sent to Chen Bangrong while waiting at the police station, it can be seen that Chen Jian had indeed reached a consensus with Chen Jing and others to wait until dawn and go to court to resolve the dispute. Furthermore, the police station and the nearby Chongqing Fanghua Hospital had staff on duty at all times. If Chen Jian believed his personal freedom was restricted or his physical or mental health was harmed or threatened, he could have immediately sought protection and assistance. There is no evidence in the case that Chen Jian sought protection or assistance, nor any evidence that Chen Jian suffered harm from Wu Jianping or Li Yueguo. Therefore, the Chongqing No. 1 Intermediate People’s Court held that the appellees did not engage in any tortious act that exceeded legal norms and directly infringed upon another person’s body, leading to the consequences of this case.

Throughout the entire process, there was no fault—neither intent nor negligence—in the conduct of the appellees Chen Jing and others. The purpose of Chen Jing’s side was clear: to realize their lawful creditor’s rights. On one hand, they called the police, contacted the enforcement judge, and went together to the police station to explain the situation. On the other hand, while waiting at the police station, they closely monitored Chen Jian’s movements, even following and waiting for him when he went to the restroom, to ensure that they could go to court together after dawn to resolve the enforcement of the case. The fact that Chen Jian ultimately jumped out of the restroom window demonstrated the necessity of the aforementioned conduct. Throughout the entire process, the appellees had no intent or negligence to infringe on Chen Jian’s right to life, nor could they have anticipated Chen Jian’s death. Therefore, the Chongqing No. 1 Intermediate People’s Court held that, under the circumstances where the debtor had failed to perform his legal obligation for years and the creditor’s rights could never be realized, Chen Jing’s side took measures to prevent the debtor from concealing himself again. These were legitimate acts to protect their own lawful rights and interests and did not exceed the legal limits; thus, there was no fault.

The conduct of the appellees Chen Jing and others was neither illegal nor faulty, and it was not causally related to Chen Jian’s death. As an adult, Chen Jian should have had sufficient awareness of the potential consequences of jumping out of a window. Moreover, as analyzed above, even if his personal safety were truly threatened, he could have sought proper protection and should have compared and judged the possible harm from such threats against the harm from jumping out of a window. The Chongqing No. 1 Intermediate People’s Court held that the appellees’ conduct did not necessarily cause Chen Jian to jump to his death. There was no causal relationship between Chen Jian’s death and the appellees’ conduct.

In summary, the appeal of the appellants Chen Bangrong, Chen Guorong, and Chen Xi could not be sustained and should be dismissed. The first-instance judgment had clear findings of fact and correct application of law and should be affirmed. Accordingly, the Chongqing No. 1 Intermediate People’s Court, in accordance with Article 170(1)(1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People’s Republic of China, rendered its judgment on May 16, 2018:

The appeal was dismissed, and the original judgment was affirmed.

This judgment is final.
